turns.content: Before treatment, the inhibition zones were 25 mm for ampicillin, 23 mm for azithromycin, and 5 mm for meropenem. Using susceptible cutoffs of 17, 15, and 10 mm, respectively, how should the isolate be classified?
After ethidium-bromide treatment, the zones were 25, 23, and 13 mm in the same order. What changed?
There was only one before/after run, with no untreated control, replicate, plasmid profile, or gene-specific PCR. What can the experiment establish?
Given those limitations, should the observed change be interpreted as causal or only associative?
What mechanism could plausibly explain the phenotype change without treating it as established?
What can be concluded about the location of the meropenem-resistance determinant?
